processing: Server-reprojected to Mars 2000 sphere geographic degrees; generalized 0.03 degree for regional visualization; not survey precision.

uniqueValueInfos.label: Amazonian and Hesperian transition undivided unit
Hesperian and Noachian highland undivided unit

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Hummocky and pitted at meter (northern cap) to hundreds of meter (southern cap) scales. Very high albedo except on pit floors. Mostly <2 m (northern cap) to <10 m (southern cap) thick. (lat 83.00° N., long 317.85° E. and lat –86.04° N., long 291.81° E.)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Thinly caps parts of Planum Boreum and Planum Australe. Superposes units Apu and Hpu. Location of unit margin varies and south polar surface pits enlarge seasonally and annually
attributes.Interpretation: Residual ice (H2O in northern cap and mainly CO2 in southern cap) with dust lags trapped in north polar pits. Margins and surface of unit actively changing due to ice accumulation and ablation

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Shields and cones having summit and flank depressions in polar regions. Relatively low radar dielectric constant. Hundreds of meters thick. (lat 75.94° N., long 206.23° E. and lat –75.96° N., long 341.69° E.)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Forms Scandia Tholi and Sisyphi Tholus. Gradational with units Hp and lHl; overlain by units mAl, Apu, and lApd. Rugged texture
attributes.Interpretation: Cryovolcanic or sedimentary or igneous volcanic, ice-rich constructs. Highly degraded by mass wasting and (or) sublimation

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Plains-forming deposits marked by narrow sinuous, anabranching ridges and irregular depressions. Relatively low radar dielectric constant. Hundreds of meters thick. (lat –77.78° N., long 332.51° E.; locality 48)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Surrounds Planum Australe. Superposes units lNh, lNv, mNh, and eNh; gradational with unit Hpe; overlain by units Ap and Apu. Bumpy surface at meter scale
attributes.Interpretation: Water-ice sheets as indicated by dielectric constant, perhaps emplaced by cryovolcanism or from atmospheric precipitation. Covered by thin, periglacially deformed mantling deposit

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Uneven to rolling topography; high-relief outcrops that extend hundreds to thousands of kilometers. Commonly layered in crater walls. May be hundreds of meters to more than a kilometer thick. (lat –47.17° N., long 349.33° E.; localities 7, 14, 19, 20, 22, 23, 31)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Extensive in the equatorial to southern highlands. Superposes units eNh and eNhm; gradational with units mNhm, Nhu, Nhe, Nve, and HNt and ANa (Noachian parts); overlain by units lNh, lNv, HNt (Hesperian part), HNhu, HNb, eHb, eHv, eHh, eHt, Hp, Ht, Hto, Htu, lHl, lHv, lHvf, ANa, AHtu, AHv, Apu, mAl, and lAv. Heavily cratered and marked by locally dense valleys, grabens, and wrinkle ridges
attributes.Interpretation: Undifferentiated impact, volcanic, fluvial, and basin materials. Moderately to heavily degraded

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Craters with rims and surrounding blankets; some include single to multi-lobed blanket forms, dense secondary crater chains, and (or) central peak or pit. Blanket thicknesses of meters to a few hundred meters. (lat 23.17° N., long 207.77° E.
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Global occurrence. Superposes Noachian units; other unit superposition relations diverse. High kilometer-scale surface roughness; crater floors may be smooth to rough
attributes.Interpretation: Upturned, ejected, and brecciated target rocks and sediments, with local areas of impact melt. Post-impact mass-wasting and fluvial-lacustrine and eolian infill of craters common

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Plateaus hundreds of kilometers across at both poles. Moderate to high albedo. Meters-thick layers; some internal unconformities; local lower, mostly low-albedo deposits unevenly bedded or crossbedded. Exceeds 1,000 m thickness in places. (lat 80.97° N., long 0.00° E. and lat –83.15° N., long 64.91° E.)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Forms Planum Australe and upper part of Planum Boreum. Superposes units lHl, Hp, Hpe, Hpu, lNh, mNh, eNh, and most of Ap; overlain by unit lApc and, except for youngest part, by unit lApd. Tens-of-meters-thick layers in radargrams; modified by systems of spiral and aligned troughs
attributes.Interpretation: Water ice with minor amounts of dust intermixed and as lags; local lower sequences made up of frozen dunes with interbedded ice layers

attributes.Interpretation: Undifferentiated friable sedimentary, impact, and volcanic materials. Tectonically contracted in places

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Planar deposits meters to tens of meters thick and tens to hundreds of kilometers across; lobate scarps common. Variable daytime IR brightness in places. Hundreds of meters or more total thickness. (lat –25.34° N., long 279.97° E.; localities 38, 42)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: High plains within and near Tharsis rise, Syrtis Major and Hesperia Plana, and Gusev crater. Marked by wrinkle ridges
attributes.Interpretation: Flood lavas, undifferentiated, sourced from regional fissure and vent systems. Tectonically contracted

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Shield-like edifices several tens to hundreds of kilometers across; lobate flow morphologies indistinct or absent. As much as few kilometers thick. (lat –8.11° N., long 174.50° E.)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Occurrences include Amphitrites and Peneus Paterae, Tyrrhenus Mons, northern Apollinaris Mons, and southern Tharsis rise. Heavily cratered; some outcrops have summit depressions tens of kilometers across; marked by irregular scarps and ridges; some radiating valleys
attributes.Interpretation: Volcanic edifices composed of different combinations of lava flows, pyroclastic deposits, and volcaniclastic deposits sourced from degraded shields. Domed and fractured by local intrusions. Tectonically contracted

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Irregular plateaus hundreds of kilometers across. Layered. Hundreds of meters to kilometers thick. (lat –6.41° N., long 156.42° E; lat –6.17° N., long 286.05° E.; localities 26, 28)

attributes.UnitDesc: Hesperian and Noachian highland undivided unit
attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Mound forming. Light toned in visible images. Layered. Hundreds of meters to several kilometers thick. (lat 5.97° N., long 2.33° E.; locality 24)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Occurs on Meridiani Planum, in some highland craters, and east of Hellas Planitia. Includes hydrated sulfate spectral signatures
attributes.Interpretation: Undifferentiated, friable (likely fine grained) sedimentary, volcanic, and impact rocks. Altered by weathering

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Plains-forming deposits, relatively smooth; includes small knobs and mesas of Noachian and perhaps younger material. May be tens to hundreds of meters thick. (lat 18.13° N., long 117.11° E.; localities 8, 15)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Occurs along highland/lowland boundary, near Phlegra Montes, on and alongside Valles Marineris and on several crater floors, and at Acidalia Mensa and southeast of Hesperia Planum. Superposes units eHt, eHv, eHh, Htu, HNt, Nhu, mNh, mNhm, and eNh; gradational with unit Hve; interfingers with unit AHv, overlain by units Hto, lHl, AHtu, Aa, mAl, lAv, and younger part of ANa. Moderate density of wrinkle ridges; dense branching valleys near Echus Chasma
attributes.Interpretation: Mass-wasting, fluvial/lacustrine, and possibly other sedimentary materials and volcanic rocks in places. Tectonically contracted

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Lobes bounded by scarps tens to hundreds of kilometers across, marked by transverse ridges few kilometers wide and tens of kilometers long; linear grooves in places. As much as 1,000 m thick. (lat –8.04° N., long 281.80° E. and lat 30.17° N., long 214.65° E.)

attributes.UnitDesc: Amazonian and Hesperian transition undivided unit
attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Irregularly shaped plateaus hundreds to more than one thousand kilometers across. Locally layered. Hundreds of meters to ~3,000 m thick.  (lat –2.37° N., long 240.33° E.; localities 25, 27, 30)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Occurs along highland/lowland boundary from Olympus Mons to southwestern Elysium Planitia and as one small outcrop west of Kasei Valles. Superposes units Aa, Ave, lHv, lHt, eHv, eHt, Htu, HNt, Nve, mNh, and eNh; interfingers with unit AHv; overlain by unit lAv. Marked by dense linear ridges, grooves, and scarps hundreds of meters wide and tens of kilometers long; includes subdued and pedestal-crater forms
attributes.Interpretation: Fine-grained eolian sediments and (or) pyroclastic air-fall deposits. Linear ridges and grooves form yardangs

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Plains-forming deposits, undulating to moderately rugged; includes scattered low knobs and mesas of Noachian highland material. May be tens to hundreds of meters thick. (lat 13.38° N., long 116.70° E.; localities 2, 16)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Abutting the highland/lowland boundary, Arcadia and southwestern Amazonis Planitiae, and Acidalia Mensa. Moderate density of wrinkle ridges
attributes.Interpretation: Mass-wasting, fluvial/lacustrine, and other sedimentary materials and possibly volcanic rocks in places. Tectonically contracted

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Lobate flows, meters to tens of meters thick and tens to hundreds of kilometers long; forms patches hundreds to more than a thousand kilometers across. Variable daytime IR brightness in places. Hundreds of meters or more total thickness. (lat –18.84° N., long 256.12° E.; localities 17, 29)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Distributed occurrence in Tharsis region, southwestern Hesperia Planum, and Orcus Patera. Superposes units eHv, eHh, lNh, Nhu, Nhe, Nve, mNh, eNh, and eNhm; gradational with units lHvf and Hve; overlain by units AHv, AHtu, ANa (Amazonian part), Aa, lAv, and lAvf. Largest patch in Syria Planum region deeply dissected by troughs and grabens of Noctis Labyrinthus and Noctis Fossae
attributes.Interpretation: Flood lavas and large lava flows, undifferentiated, sourced from regional fissure and vent systems

attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Occurs along highland/lowland boundary from Olympus Mons to southwestern Elysium Planitia and as one small outcrop west of Kasei Valles. attributes.Interpretation: Fine-grained eolian sediments and (or) pyroclastic air-fall deposits. Linear ridges and grooves form yardangs

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Craters with rims and surrounding blankets; some include single to multi-lobed blanket forms, dense secondary crater chains, and (or) central peak or pit. Blanket thicknesses of meters to a few hundred meters. (lat 23.17° N., long 207.77° E.

attributes.Interpretation: Upturned, ejected, and brecciated target rocks and sediments, with local areas of impact melt. Post-impact mass-wasting and fluvial-lacustrine and eolian infill of craters common

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Mostly plains forming, rugged in places. May be hundreds of meters thick. (lat –20.74° N., long 354.35° E.; localities 13, 34, 35)

attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Covers Chryse Planitia, eastern Lunae Planum, and canyons in Xanthe and Margaritifer Terrae. Superposes units AHv, lHt, eHh, eHv, eHt, lNh, mNh, Nhu, and eNh; gradational with unit Ht; overlain by unit lHl
attributes.Interpretation: Outflow channel fluvial and debris-flow deposits from catastrophic erosion of highland rocks; islands of underlying bedrock exposed

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Lobes bounded by scarps tens to hundreds of kilometers across, marked by transverse ridges few kilometers wide and tens of kilometers long; linear grooves in places. As much as 1,000 m thick. (lat –8.04° N., long 281.80° E. and lat 30.17° N., long 214.65° E.)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Surrounds Olympus Mons and covers parts of walls and floors of Valles Marineris. Superposes units Av, lHt, lHv, eHh, Ht, Htu, lNh, lNv, and Nhu; overlain by units lAv, lAa, lAvf, AHtu, and youngest part of Ave
attributes.Interpretation: Landslide and gravity-spreading deposits derived from flanks of Olympus Mons and walls of Valles Marineris

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Shield-like edifices several tens to hundreds of kilometers across; made up of lobate flows meters to tens of meters thick and tens to hundreds of kilometers across, as well as dissected layers tens of meters thick. As much as few kilometers thick. (lat 24.65° N., long 146.80° E.)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Occurs at Tharsis and Elysium rises, Hadriacus Mons, and Apollinaris Mons south flank. Superposes unit eNhm; gradational with units lHv, lHvf, lHt, lHl, eHv, and HNt (Hesperian part); overlain by unit AHv. Some outcrops have summit calderas tens of kilometers across; some radiating valleys
attributes.Interpretation: Volcanic edifices composed of different combinations of lava flows and pyroclastic and volcaniclastic deposits. Modified by summit collapse from magma withdrawal and fluvial dissection in places

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: High-relief massifs tens of kilometers across separated by broad linear troughs and valleys. Kilometers thick. (lat –44.48° N., long 307.54° E.)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Surrounds Argyre and part of Isidis Planitiae. Gradational with units mNh, eNh, and HNt (Noachian part); overlain by units lNh, HNb, HNt (Hesperian part), eHh, eHt, eHv, lHt, and lHl. Heavily cratered; dissected by grabens and valleys in places
attributes.Interpretation: Ancient, degraded crustal rocks uplifted by large, basin-forming impacts. Dissected by basin-related fault structures and erosional valleys

attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Distributed occurrence in Syria Planum, western Tempe Terra, southwest of Ceraunius Fossae, western Elysium Mons, and Orcus Patera. attributes.Interpretation: Volcanoes and lava flows

Moderate density of wrinkle ridges
attributes.Interpretation: Mass-wasting, fluvial/lacustrine, and other sedimentary materials and possibly volcanic rocks in places. Tectonically contracted

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Planar to undulating; lobate and troughed marginal areas in places. Hundreds of meters to kilometers thick. (lat 21.40° N., long 118.20° E.; localities 1, 6, 10, 11)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Continuous across most of the northern plains. Embays units lHt, Hto, eHt, eHv, HNt, lNh, mNhm, and mNh; superposed by units AHv, Av, eAb, Apu, mAl, lAv, and lApd; temporal relation to units Hpe and Hpu unclear. Contains hundreds of superposed pedestal-crater forms, thumbprint terrain, topographically subdued wrinkle ridges, and narrow grabens northeast of Alba Mons
attributes.Interpretation: Fluvial/lacustrine/marine and colluvial sediments sourced from circum-lowland outflow channels and bounding highland terrains; likely intercalated with and underlain by lava and volcaniclastic rocks. Pervasively modified and obscured by periglaciation, sedimentary diapirism, and particulate mantling

attributes.Interpretation: Flood lavas and large lava flows, undifferentiated, sourced from regional fissure and vent systems. Highly variable ages of individual flows, although generally younger in central parts of Tharsis rise

Contains hundreds of superposed pedestal-crater forms, thumbprint terrain, topographically subdued wrinkle ridges, and narrow grabens northeast of Alba Mons
attributes.Interpretation: Fluvial/lacustrine/marine and colluvial sediments sourced from circum-lowland outflow channels and bounding highland terrains; likely intercalated with and underlain by lava and volcaniclastic rocks. Pervasively modified and obscured by periglaciation, sedimentary diapirism, and particulate mantling

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Craters with rims and surrounding blankets; some include single to multi-lobed blanket forms, dense secondary crater chains, and (or) central peak or pit. Blanket thicknesses of meters to a few hundred meters. (lat 23.17° N., long 207.77° E.
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Global occurrence. Superposes Noachian units; other unit superposition relations diverse. High kilometer-scale surface roughness; crater floors may be smooth to rough
attributes.Interpretation: Upturned, ejected, and brecciated target rocks and sediments, with local areas of impact melt. Post-impact mass-wasting and fluvial-lacustrine and eolian infill of craters common

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Shields and cones having summit and flank depressions in polar regions. Relatively low radar dielectric constant. Hundreds of meters thick. (lat 75.94° N., long 206.23° E. and lat –75.96° N., long 341.69° E.)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Forms Scandia Tholi and Sisyphi Tholus. Gradational with units Hp and lHl; overlain by units mAl, Apu, and lApd. Rugged texture
attributes.Interpretation: Cryovolcanic or sedimentary or igneous volcanic, ice-rich constructs. Highly degraded by mass wasting and (or) sublimation

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Mounds with barchan-like, linear, and other dune morphologies. Low albedo. Marked by meter-scale ripples. Mounds typically tens to hundreds of meters across and tens of meters high. (lat 81.21° N., long 217.34° E.)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Surrounds Planum Boreum. Superposes units mAl, lHl, Hpe, and most of Apu. Includes spectral detections of sulfates, including gypsum
attributes.Interpretation: Wind-blown sand organized into variety of dune forms owing to variable wind activity and permafrost development

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Plateaus hundreds of kilometers across at both poles. Moderate to high albedo. Meters-thick layers; some internal unconformities; local lower, mostly low-albedo deposits unevenly bedded or crossbedded. Exceeds 1,000 m thickness in places. (lat 80.97° N., long 0.00° E. and lat –83.15° N., long 64.91° E.)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Forms Planum Australe and upper part of Planum Boreum. Superposes units lHl, Hp, Hpe, Hpu, lNh, mNh, eNh, and most of Ap; overlain by unit lApc and, except for youngest part, by unit lApd. Tens-of-meters-thick layers in radargrams; modified by systems of spiral and aligned troughs
attributes.Interpretation: Water ice with minor amounts of dust intermixed and as lags; local lower sequences made up of frozen dunes with interbedded ice layers

attributes.Interpretation: Ice-rich loess. Periglacial modification formed thumbprint terrain

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Plateau-forming deposits. Decameter-thick layers. Relatively low radar dielectric constant. Locally >1,000 m thick. (lat 80.28° N., long 302.72° E.)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Forms base of main lobe of Planum Boreum, including Rupes Tenuis and mouth of Chasma Boreale. Moderately low radar dielectric constant. Overlain by units Apu, lApd, and lApc; stratigraphic relation to unit lHl uncertain. Lower sequences locally cut by polygonal troughs; contains local pedestal crater forms
attributes.Interpretation: Roughly equal proportions of water ice and lithic fines, possibly emplaced during lowland flooding events or by eolian activity. Deeply eroded but armored by impact material; lower sequence troughed likely due to compaction

attributes.PrimaryCharacteristics: Hummocky and pitted at meter (northern cap) to hundreds of meter (southern cap) scales. Very high albedo except on pit floors. Mostly <2 m (northern cap) to <10 m (southern cap) thick. (lat 83.00° N., long 317.85° E. and lat –86.04° N., long 291.81° E.)
attributes.AdditionalCharacteristics: Thinly caps parts of Planum Boreum and Planum Australe. Superposes units Apu and Hpu. Location of unit margin varies and south polar surface pits enlarge seasonally and annually
attributes.Interpretation: Residual ice (H2O in northern cap and mainly CO2 in southern cap) with dust lags trapped in north polar pits. Margins and surface of unit actively changing due to ice accumulation and ablation
